Theme

Latin word

deinde

adverb; after prīmum

secondly, next (in a list of points); then, next, after that

In this lexicon

  • secondly

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 6.3.1: prīmum quod vidētur esse honōs … deinde quod sōlum habeō praetōrium; Ter. Heaut. 3: Id prīmum dīcam: deinde quod vēnī ēloquar.

  • then

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. S. 1.6.119: deinde eō dormītum; Catull. 5.7–9; Cic. Or. 154: dein … prō deinde … dīcimus; Traupman 37, 351; Traupman 205; Traupman 206

Examples

  • prīmum est dēvium, deinde ab Autrōniō et cēterīs quadriduī, deinde sine tē.

    Firstly, it’s off the road; secondly, it’s four days from Autronius and the rest; and thirdly, it’s without you.Cic. Att. 3.7.1

    In the entry for secondly

  • Id prīmum dīcam: deinde quod vēnī ēloquar.

    I’ll explain that first; then I’ll say what I’ve come for.Ter. Heaut. 3

    In the entry for secondly

  • quid fit deinde?

    and then what happens?Plaut. Amph. 1098

    In the entry for then

  • dā mī bāsia mīlle, deinde centum, dein mīlle altera, dein secunda centum

    give me a thousand kisses, then a hundred, then another thousand, then a second hundredCatull. 5.7–9

    In the entry for then

  • Homō est prīmum īnfāns, deinde puer, tum adulēscēns, inde juvenis, posteā vir, dehinc senex, tandem silicernium.

    A person is first a baby, then a boy, then a youth, then a young man, then a man, then an old man, and at last a doddering ancient.Comen. OP 36

    In the entry for then
